instruction: Open the Navigator panel in LibreOffice Impress.

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(5); pyautogui.press('esc'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('f10'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('right', presses=2, interval=0.1); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.press('down', presses=11, interval=0.1); pyautogui.press('enter')

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully restored the hidden left slide panel by navigating View menu and clicking 'Slide Pane'. Completed in 5 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate View menu in LibreOffice Impress, identify and toggle UI panel visibility options, understand Impress layout panels
metadata.task_rationale: Model demonstrated ability to find and use View menu options. Opening the Navigator (View > Navigator) requires the same menu navigation skill but targets a different panel, adding variety while staying within proven capabilities.
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening the Navigator panel via View > Navigator (Shift+Ctrl+F5). The evaluator checks the accessibility tree for the presence of 'Navigator' text, indicating the panel is open. Returns 1.0 if found, 0.0 otherwise.

llm_judge_reasons: Instruction is a single-step task (open Navigator panel) and the evaluator checks for its presence in the accessibility tree — coverage is complete.
Getter (accessibility_tree) correctly extracts the UI state needed to verify whether the Navigator panel is open.
Metric logic is straightforward: checks for 'Navigator' substring in the accessibility tree string, returning 1.0 if found.

Minor concern: simple substring match for 'Navigator' could produce false positives if the word appears in other UI elements (menu items, tooltips) even when the panel is not open. A more robust check would look for a Navigator frame/panel role specifically.

The expected parameter {'navigator_visible': true} is received correctly per framework rules (get_rule returns config['rules']), but is never actually used by the metric function — effectively dead configuration.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Make the accessibility tree check more specific by searching for a Navigator panel/frame/window role rather than a plain substring match, to reduce false positive risk.
Consider using the expected parameter to make the metric more configurable, or simplify expected to just a string type if the rules dict is unused.
